role: The world config reader and key registry (lane/worldyaml): parses config.yaml (or configs/NAME.yaml) by the strict YAML subset its header writes down, or a tape header on replay (world object, options.difficulty and options.rd), plus --set section.key=value (a bare key is a world key); KEYS lists every key with its default and kind (world: seed, difficulty, render_distance, daylight_cycle, keep_inventory, villages and the UNSUPPORTED switches; client: graphics, particles, observation, ticks_per_step, hud; engine: device_mesh, device_generation, device_light; pipeline: kind, start), refusing unknown keys and values. Forces every UNSUPPORTED key off with a notice, sets a seed start's non-vanilla game rules at its first server tick (atServerTick), exposes the public booleans vanilla hooks check, refuses /summon of switched-off entities and prunes horses, wolves and ocelots from every biome spawn list.
used_by: oracle/harness/netherite/oracle/Main.java (--conf, --set; the difficulty, render distance, particles and graphics defaults of options.txt) and the tape header (json())
csrc/engine/worldconf.c (the same grammar and registry in C)
csrc/engine/spawning.c and csrc/engine/seedworld_creatures.h (spawn lists after pruneSpawns)
notes: vanilla_hooks is every oracle/src file that names WorldConf (grep); what each hook gates was not read per file. Unknown keys and values outside a key's kind are errors. Main.java calls WorldConf.load(conf, sets, Oracle.replayPath) and Checkpoint.verify uses WorldConf.json(). json() writes a game rule only when it is not vanilla's, so every tape before the rules reads the same; difficulty and render distance stay in the header's options (1.7.10 client options, applied as the integrated server starts).
